name: Peloponnes
summary: Civilization building and auction game where players bid for land and buildings over 8 rounds to grow population and wealth.
rules_text: Each player has a mat tracking wood, stone, food, population, luxury and coins. Setup gives each a random civilization with starting resources and coins. Play lasts 8 rounds. Each round: reveal as many land/building tiles as players plus tiles to fill a 5-tile display including a Conquest Row. Tiles have minimum bids; Conquest Row costs +3 and cannot be outbid. In turn order, players bid by placing coins face-down under a tile with their marker. If outbid, player must move his exact bid to another tile, or withdraw and take his bid plus 1 coin from bank, or pass for 3 coins. After all bid, turn order for next round is descending bid amount. Players collect tiles, pay wood/stone to build buildings or place a coin debt, and must match at least one resource icon when placing land tiles. Then gain one-time population and coins and then round income from all tiles. Finally reveal two disaster chits; when three of one type appear, its disaster hits.
rating_reason: Civ auction and development, bidding, turn-based strategic.
reasons: capability: conditional_subsequence: the step list is flat: a whole BLOCK of steps cannot be chosen instead of another block. This is NOT a limit on conditional scoring or conditional updates: a single step can carry a `when` condition and a single operation an `if`, both arithmetic, so 'the poisoner scores if the choices match, otherwise the chooser' is fine
capability: trading_between_players: no mechanism for a player to propose and a player to accept an exchange
